b05.evidence: The long upper and lower horizontals and doubled oblique support double-struck Z. b06.evidence: The sign after donc has only a tiny lower body and a detached upper mark. The lower body is too reduced to distinguish accented à from two punctuation points with confidence. Retain à first and colon as an alternative.

b07.evidence: The Z has one thick diagonal whose possible doubled trace cannot be separated; the existing double-struck/plain doubt remains. Both A letters, parentheses, one-wave equivalence and comma agree.

b08.evidence: A has a clear final triangular body and right leg over the old diagonal/horizontal Z remnants. Keep the old Z alphabet doubtful within deletion and the replacement A explicit. The second reader’s wider unsure wrapper does not require removing the visible replacement.

b09.evidence: The apparent dark stroke in des follows the loop and retracing of its d. There is no independent cancellation extending across the whole word and no second live les. Retain des live.

b10.decision: retain uncertain words; qualify terminal comma
b10.evidence: The cancelled words have recognizable tall l/t and inductives strokes but low bodies merge with the cancellation, so their doubt stays. A short dark oblique descends at the right end beyond the final letter returns; a cancelled comma is possible, though its meeting with the strike prevents certainty. Record it as unsure. b11.evidence: Both readings preserve des/de uncertainty and the same words; the curly versus straight apostrophe is typographical.

b12.evidence: The compressed onset has an isolated low mark and joined returns; avec remains favored, but the crop does not resolve the existing ou alternative. Do not remove the doubt from the independent reader’s certainty alone.

b13.evidence: The first sign is reduced to a short slanted lower stroke and a detached upper mark, comparable to b06. Keep à/colon unresolved; la and underlined van Kampen, including its final comma, are clear.

b14.evidence: The lower stroke has a single downward return at its right end, without the second converging flank of an arrowhead. It differs from the true arrow below the inserted Lim in b10. Retain capital underlined Lim.

b15.evidence: The two tiny points below the end of Topos are far below the writing baseline and have no stable punctuation placement; they are not added as a colon. The final short word has an e onset and compressed s before the terminal t return, supporting est. Both capital T forms and the ordinary quotation strokes remain.

b16.evidence: The right end of the lower stroke turns down once; it does not form two converging arrowhead strokes. Retain the underline, consistently with b14 and in contrast with the clear arrow in b10.
